verses.text: Jesus was born in Bethlehem, Judea, while Herod was king. Around then, some wise men from the east pulled into Jerusalem.
“Where is the child born to be King of the Jews? We saw his star rise in the east, and we came to worship him.”
When King Herod heard that, he was shaken—and Jerusalem was shaken right along with him.
He gathered all the chief priests and teachers of the law and asked them where the Messiah was to be born.
They told him, “In Bethlehem, Judea. The prophet wrote:
‘Bethlehem, in Judah’s land, you are by no means the least among Judah’s rulers. From you will come a ruler who will shepherd my people Israel.’”
Then Herod secretly called the wise men in and got the exact time the star had appeared.
He sent them to Bethlehem: “Go and search carefully for the child. When you find him, report back to me so I can go worship him too.”
They heard the king and set out. The star they had seen in the east went ahead of them until it stopped over the place where the child was.
When they saw the star, joy hit them hard—they were overjoyed! 🌟
They went into the house and saw the child with Mary his mother. They bowed down and worshiped him; then they opened their treasures and gave him gold, frankincense, and myrrh.
They were warned in a dream not to go back to Herod, so they returned to their own country by another route.

After they left, an angel of the Lord appeared to Joseph in a dream: “Get up. Take the child and his mother and escape to Egypt. Stay there till I tell you, because Herod is about to search for the child and kill him.”
Joseph got up, took the child and his mother that night, and left for Egypt.
He stayed there until Herod died. That fulfilled what the Lord had said through the prophet: “I called my son out of Egypt.”

Herod realized the wise men had outsmarted him, and he was furious. He sent men to kill every boy in Bethlehem and its surrounding area who was two years old or younger, using the exact time he had learned from the wise men.
Then what Jeremiah the prophet had said came true:
“A cry was heard in Ramah—people grieving, weeping, and mourning deeply. Rachel was weeping for her children; nobody could comfort her, because they were gone.”
After Herod died, an angel of the Lord appeared to Joseph in a dream in Egypt.
“Get up. Take the child and his mother and go to the land of Israel,” the angel said, “because the people trying to kill the child are dead.”
Joseph got up, took the child and his mother, and went to Israel.
But he heard that Archelaus was ruling Judea in place of his father Herod, and he was afraid to go there. Warned in a dream, he went away to the region of Galilee.
He settled in a town called Nazareth. That fulfilled what the prophets had said: “He will be called a Nazarene.”
